root_cause: The dropdown's keydown handler calls event.stopPropagation() for all dropdown commands, including Escape. When focus is on the access toggle button (the dropdown toggle), pressing Escape triggers the dropdown handler, which stops propagation, preventing the modal's Escape handler from receiving the event and closing the dialog.
repair_strategy: Modify the dropdown's dataApiKeydownHandler to conditionally stop propagation: only stop propagation for Escape if the event originates from within the dropdown menu (i.e., event.target.closest('.dropdown-menu')). This allows Escape pressed on the dropdown toggle button to bubble to the modal, closing the dialog, while preserving the behavior that Escape inside the open dropdown menu closes only the menu.
expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape while focus is on the access toggle button will close the share dialog, making the button invisible. Pressing Escape while focus is inside the open dropdown menu will close only the menu, leaving the dialog open.
functional_risks: If other components rely on the dropdown's Escape key stopping propagation globally, they may receive the event unexpectedly.
The selector '.dropdown-menu' relies on Bootstrap's internal class name; if the dropdown implementation changes, this may need updating.
verification_requirements: Verify Escape closes the modal when focus is on the access toggle button.
Verify Escape closes only the dropdown menu when focus is on a dropdown menu item.
Verify that after closing the dropdown menu with Escape, focus returns to the access toggle button.
Verify that the modal can still be closed by Escape when focus is elsewhere in the modal (e.g., on the Cancel button).
Verify that the regression guard 'Escape inside the open access menu closes only the menu' passes.
